evals.name: gradebook-sync-from-docs
evals.prompt: Here's the data dictionary and architecture notes for Gradebook Sync. Can you turn it into a RoPA entry?
evals.expected_output: A processor entry (Provisional) for the sync, led by the Art. 30(2) fields, with the districts' purposes marked controller-to-confirm and the model's purpose left open as possibly the company's own (Art. 28(10)). Data elements only from the dictionary. iep_flag flagged special category (Provisional, with a reason); ell_status not special category by itself. Children and education-record flags. Recipients: AWS, the error monitoring vendor, and the districts' LMSs. Backups 35 days; indefinite sync logs and payload capture turned into actions; other retention TBC. Transfers screened or TBC, not decided by where students live. Follow-ons: dpia, vendor reviews, ai-intake. Reply about 150 words plus at most five Round 1 questions.
expectations: `gov validate` reports 0 errors after the run
`gov render --check` reports everything up to date
Every .md file under compliance/registers/ropa/ has a matching .yaml record (no hand-written Markdown)
The entry's ID was allocated by gov (compliance/.gov/counters.yaml covers it)
record_type is processor or both, Provisional, and every district-decided purpose has lawful basis controller-to-confirm
The model's scoring purpose is open as possibly the company's own purpose, through decided_by TBC or company, a question, or a linked controller entry
Every data element listed appears in the data dictionary; none are added
iep_flag is flagged special category with Provisional status and a reason
ell_status is not flagged special category on its own
AWS, the error monitoring vendor, and the districts or their LMSs are recipients
Backups show 35 days, and other retention without a source is TBC
Indefinite sync logs or full-payload capture appear as an action with an owner, not only as a question
Transfers are TBC or screened by flow (regime, exporter, importer, access); none is decided from where students live
Follow-ons recommend dpia and ai-intake
The reply, excluding its numbered question list, is 200 words or fewer
The reply's numbered question list has five questions or fewer
The reply doesn't present `gov validate` as legal approval

evals.name: hr-onboarding-interview
evals.prompt: Add HR onboarding to the RoPA. We collect new hire name, home address, SSN or PPSN, bank details, emergency contacts, I-9 documents, and background check results. Workday holds it; Checkr runs background checks. Staff are in the US and Ireland. HR owns it.
evals.expected_output: Controller entry or entries (Provisional) for HR onboarding; one entry or linked US and Irish entries are both acceptable. Purposes split. Lawful bases Provisional, with reasons. Background checks flagged criminal, with Art. 10 for Irish staff raised. Emergency contacts as third-party subjects. Ireland-to-US flows via Workday and Checkr screened with the mechanism TBC. No data elements beyond what the user listed. Retention TBC, with any legal requirement kept apart from practice. Vendor reviews for Workday and Checkr. Reply about 150 words plus at most five Round 1 questions.
expectations: `gov validate` reports 0 errors after the run
`gov render --check` reports everything up to date
Every .md file under compliance/registers/ropa/ has a matching .yaml record (no hand-written Markdown)
The entry's ID was allocated by gov (compliance/.gov/counters.yaml covers it)
Every entry's record_type is controller, Provisional
Purposes are split, with separate rows for at least payroll or hiring, right-to-work checks, and background screening
Background check data is flagged criminal, and an open question or verify flag raises Art. 10 for Irish staff
Emergency contacts are recorded as third-party data subjects
Ireland-to-US flows through Workday or Checkr are listed with the mechanism TBC or sourced, never assumed
No data element is recorded beyond those the user listed; anything more specific, such as IBAN, appears only as a question
Every retention period is TBC or sourced, and any legal requirement sits apart from current practice
Follow-ons recommend vendor reviews for Workday and Checkr
US background checks through Checkr raise FCRA disclosure, authorization, or adverse-action steps in a question, verify flag, or action
The reply, excluding its numbered question list, is 200 words or fewer
The reply's numbered question list has five questions or fewer
The reply doesn't present `gov validate` as legal approval
